sections.content:
77,130 people

were counted on the census as "specialist medical practitioners" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Specialist medical practitioners specialise in particular areas of modern medicine. Their work involves diagnosing mental and physical injuries, disorders and diseases within their specialism, prescribing and giving treatment, recommending preventative action, and conducting medical education and research activities.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 40 to 44 years. Of the whole working population 10.9% were aged 40 to 44 years. For people working as "specialist medical practitioners", 16.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "specialist medical practitioners" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "specialist medical practitioners" included:

  • public relations and communications directors
  • functional managers and directors (other)
  • charitable organisation managers and directors

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "specialist medical practitioners" there were more men than women (58.4% compared with 41.6%).

This means "specialist medical practitioners" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 58.4% and women made up 41.6% of "specialist medical practitioners"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "specialist medical practitioners" included:

  • managers and proprietors in other services (other)
  • environment professionals
  • natural and social science professionals (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "specialist medical practitioners" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "specialist medical practitioners" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "specialist medical practitioners", 5.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (87.1% compared with 12.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (93.7%) than self-employed (6.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
